_meta.shape: LOGICAL. Pipeline maps → entity_positions (user_id=author, entity_type='proposal', entity_id=prop-hb14, stance, + statement to metadata/comment). stance ∈ support|oppose|mixed (pipeline maps to the real enum).
_meta.passive_rule: Crane (passive) posts NO position — his opposition exists only as a vote (proposals.json). That absence IS the demonstration. Statements match each official's locked HB-14 vote.
_meta.bridge_setup: ClerkEmeritus's stance is 'mixed' and his B-1 comment (threads.json) is the cross-bloc synthesis that earns the authored high bridge score.

positions.author: off-reyes-combs
positions.statement: Franklin's high country IS our economy. Clean generation plus the Just-Transition Fund is how the plateau shares in the upside instead of just bearing the cost.

positions.author: off-whitfield
positions.statement: The plateau breathes the state's worst air. Pairing this with air monitoring is overdue public health, not ideology.

positions.author: off-nandakumar
positions.statement: Transmission is grid reliability and jobs for the corridor. We build Franklin's energy future or we keep importing it at a premium.

positions.author: off-park
positions.statement: Tourism runs on a working grid and a living landscape. Both point to yes.

positions.author: off-okafor
positions.statement: I'm a yes the moment ratepayer cost recovery is capped and the transition fund is front-loaded ahead of construction. That's my Title IV amendment — earn it and you have my vote.

positions.author: off-sevier
positions.statement: Cherokee Foothills is an ex-coal county. The reinvestment piece is the first real offer Watauga has put on our table. Yes.

positions.author: off-boyd
positions.statement: I won't trade Iron Ridge's property values and ratepayers for towers whose benefit flows past us to the corridor.

positions.author: off-tipton
positions.statement: Nobody up on the ridge was asked what our skyline should look like. This is Watauga deciding for Stony Fork.

positions.author: off-hale
positions.statement: My quarrel isn't with clean power — it's Title I's land and water provisions. Fix the withdrawal and setback language and we can talk.

positions.author: cit-maziek
positions.statement: Yes — IF the transition fund comes first. The plateau has been promised retraining before and got a brochure.

positions.author: cit-ridgelinerose
positions.statement: I love these ridges and towers on them break my heart. But I read Title I's setbacks, and a heating climate breaks them worse.

positions.author: cit-oldgrowthowen
positions.statement: Our forests lose far more to a warming climate than to a carefully sited line. Support.

positions.author: cit-twokidstwoinhalers
positions.statement: Both my kids carry inhalers up here. I will take the towers, gladly.

positions.author: cit-plateaupride
positions.statement: Coal built these towns and fed my family. Don't bury that under 'transition' slideshows — show me the fund is real.

positions.author: cit-nonewtaxesned
positions.statement: Another Watauga boondoggle dressed up as 'just transition.' Hard pass.

positions.author: cit-cautiouscarla
positions.statement: With Okafor's cost cap I'm a yes. Without it the ratepayer exposure is too open-ended.

positions.author: cit-dell-r
positions.statement: Title I reaches into valley water rights. That's a no until it isn't.

positions.author: cit-clerkemeritus
positions.statement: Read Title IV. The cost cap plus fund-first sequencing is the compromise already sitting in the bill — both sides are arguing past it.
